title_as_printed: Experimental Values of CO2 Solubility x0 in Distilled Water at Pressure P and Temperature T

footnotes_as_printed.a: Combined expanded uncertainties are U(T) = 0.05 C, U(P) = 0.02 MPa, and U(x0) = 0.050 mol/kg.

pressure_note: CO2 was injected into the preheated reactor at the pressure of interest (set with an ISCO pump), 70 mL of the 100 mL autoclave filled with brine; paper does not say whether P is total or CO2 partial pressure and does not mention water vapour. U(P) = 0.02 MPa.
gas_basis_evidence: solubility reported as mol CO2 per kg (not a gas mole fraction)
mass_basis_evidence: Ca = Ct*Vt*N/Ma with Ma the mass of the titrated sample (solution) in grams; paper calls the result 'molal units (mol/kg)' and says 'the mass of solution is not a function of pressure or temperature'
conversion_needs: value unit is mol CO2 per kg; authors call it molal but derive it from the mass of the titrated sample (see mass_basis_evidence); builder must decide the kg basis
notes: Rows with a printed dash (6.2 and 21.3 MPa at 60 C) have an empty value cell (not measured). Text and abstract mention 100 C but Table 1 holds only 60 and 80 C. Text says U(x) = 0.001 mol/kg while the table footnotes say 0.050 mol/kg.
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: p.2044: Ca = Ct x Vt x N / Ma with Ma the mass of the titrated sample; 'The advantage of using mass of solution (Ma)': the printed 'molal' CO2 values are mol per kg of solution (sample), not per kg water. The sample is the NaOH-preserved mixture, so the mass basis is not strictly clean.
